purpose.statement: CSVEXPRT converts a fixed-width employee data file (employees.dat) into a comma-separated values (CSV) file (employees.csv), writing a header row followed by one CSV record per employee, and reporting the total number of records exported upon completion.

code_references.snippet:
*================================================================*
      * PROGRAM : CSVEXPRT                                             *
      * PURPOSE : CONVERT THE FIXED-WIDTH EMPLOYEE FILE TO CSV         *
      * INPUT   : data/input/employees.dat                             *
      * OUTPUT  : data/output/employees.csv                            *
      *================================================================*
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CSVEXPRT.

MAIN-PARA.
           OPEN INPUT EMP-FILE OUTPUT CSV-FILE
           MOVE "id,name,department,salary,hire_date,age" TO CSV-LINE
           WRITE CSV-LINE
           PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END PERFORM WRITE-CSV
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM
           CLOSE EMP-FILE CSV-FILE
           DISPLAY "CSVEXPRT: " WS-COUNT " RECORDS EXPORTED"
           STOP RUN.

business_rules.statement: The output CSV file must begin with a mandatory header row containing exactly these column names in order: id, name, department, salary, hire_date, age.

code_references.snippet:
MOVE "id,name,department,salary,hire_date,age" TO CSV-LINE
           WRITE CSV-LINE

business_rules.statement: Each employee's salary must be formatted as a zero-suppressed numeric value with two decimal places (up to 7 digits: 6 integer + 2 decimal) before being written to the CSV, removing leading zeros for readability.

code_references.snippet: 01  WS-SALARY-ED            PIC Z(06)9.99.
MOVE EMP-SALARY TO WS-SALARY-ED

business_rules.statement: Each employee's age must be formatted as a zero-suppressed two-digit numeric value before being written to the CSV, removing any leading zero.

code_references.snippet: 01  WS-AGE-ED               PIC Z9.
MOVE EMP-AGE    TO WS-AGE-ED

business_rules.statement: Employee name and department fields must have leading and trailing spaces trimmed before being placed in the CSV output, preventing fixed-width padding from appearing in the CSV values.

code_references.snippet:
FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-NAME)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-DEPT)        DELIMITED BY SIZE

business_rules.statement: The formatted salary value must also be trimmed of leading spaces (produced by zero-suppression editing) before being placed in the CSV output.

code_references.snippet:
FUNCTION TRIM(WS-SALARY-ED)    DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE

business_rules.statement: The hire date must be rendered in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) by concatenating the year, a literal hyphen, the month, a literal hyphen, and the day sub-fields from the employee record.

code_references.snippet:
EMP-HIRE-YYYY "-" EMP-HIRE-MM "-" EMP-HIRE-DD
                                                 DELIMITED BY SIZE

business_rules.statement: The formatted age value must be trimmed of leading spaces before being placed as the final field in the CSV output.

code_references.snippet:
","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-AGE-ED)       DELIMITED BY SIZE

business_rules.statement: Each CSV data row must be assembled into a 100-character work area that is cleared to spaces before construction, ensuring no residual data from a prior record contaminates the current output line.

code_references.snippet:
FD  CSV-FILE.
       01  CSV-LINE                PIC X(100).
MOVE SPACES TO CSV-LINE

business_rules.statement: A running count of exported employee records is maintained and incremented by one for every record successfully read and written.

code_references.snippet: 01  WS-COUNT                PIC 9(03) VALUE 0.
ADD 1 TO WS-COUNT

business_rules.statement: Processing of the input file terminates when an end-of-file condition is detected on EMP-FILE; the EOF flag is set to 'Y' via the END-OF-FILE condition-name.

code_references.snippet:
01  WS-EOF                  PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88  END-OF-FILE         VALUE 'Y'.

PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END PERFORM WRITE-CSV
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM

inputs.statement: EMP-FILE is a line-sequential fixed-width flat file located at 'data/input/employees.dat'. Its record layout is defined entirely by the EMPREC copybook, which supplies all employee field definitions (EMP-ID, EMP-NAME, EMP-DEPT, EMP-SALARY, EMP-HIRE-YYYY, EMP-HIRE-MM, EMP-HIRE-DD, EMP-AGE, etc.).

code_references.snippet:
SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/input/employees.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.

FD  EMP-FILE.
           COPY EMPREC.

outputs.statement: CSV-FILE is a line-sequential text file written to 'data/output/employees.csv'. Each record is a variable-content string held in the 100-character CSV-LINE field, containing a header row and one comma-delimited data row per employee.

code_references.snippet:
SELECT CSV-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/employees.csv"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.

FD  CSV-FILE.
       01  CSV-LINE                PIC X(100).

processing_logic.statement: STEP 1 – INITIALIZATION: Open EMP-FILE for input and CSV-FILE for output, making both files available for subsequent read and write operations.

code_references.snippet: OPEN INPUT EMP-FILE OUTPUT CSV-FILE

processing_logic.statement: STEP 2 – WRITE HEADER: Move the CSV column header string to CSV-LINE and write it as the first record of the output file.

code_references.snippet:
MOVE "id,name,department,salary,hire_date,age" TO CSV-LINE
           WRITE CSV-LINE

processing_logic.statement: STEP 3 – READ-PROCESS LOOP: Repeatedly read records from EMP-FILE until end-of-file; for each successfully read record invoke the WRITE-CSV paragraph to format and write one CSV data row.

code_references.snippet:
PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END PERFORM WRITE-CSV
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM

processing_logic.statement: STEP 4 – FORMAT RECORD (WRITE-CSV): Increment the record counter, edit salary and age into display-formatted working-storage fields, clear CSV-LINE to spaces, then STRING all employee fields — id, trimmed name, trimmed department, trimmed formatted salary, ISO-formatted hire date, and trimmed formatted age — into CSV-LINE separated by commas using a pointer-based STRING operation, then write the assembled line to CSV-FILE.

code_references.snippet:
WRITE-CSV.
           ADD 1 TO WS-COUNT
           MOVE EMP-SALARY TO WS-SALARY-ED
           MOVE EMP-AGE    TO WS-AGE-ED
           MOVE SPACES TO CSV-LINE
           MOVE 1 TO WS-PTR
           STRING EMP-ID                         DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-NAME)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ...
               INTO CSV-LINE WITH POINTER WS-PTR
           END-STRING
           WRITE CSV-LINE.

processing_logic.statement: STEP 5 – TERMINATION: Close both EMP-FILE and CSV-FILE, display the total number of exported records to the system console, and stop the run.

code_references.snippet:
CLOSE EMP-FILE CSV-FILE
           DISPLAY "CSVEXPRT: " WS-COUNT " RECORDS EXPORTED"
           STOP RUN.

dependencies.statement: EMPREC copybook defines the complete fixed-width record layout for EMP-FILE, supplying all field names referenced in WRITE-CSV (EMP-ID, EMP-NAME, EMP-DEPT, EMP-SALARY, EMP-HIRE-YYYY, EMP-HIRE-MM, EMP-HIRE-DD, EMP-AGE). The program cannot compile or function without this copybook.

code_references.snippet:
FD  EMP-FILE.
           COPY EMPREC.

STRING EMP-ID                         DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-NAME)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-DEPT)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-SALARY-ED)    DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  EMP-HIRE-YYYY "-" EMP-HIRE-MM "-" EMP-HIRE-DD
                                                 DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-AGE-ED)       DELIMITED BY SIZE

dependencies.statement: The COBOL intrinsic function TRIM is used three times in WRITE-CSV to strip leading/trailing spaces from EMP-NAME, EMP-DEPT, WS-SALARY-ED, and WS-AGE-ED. This requires a COBOL runtime that supports the TRIM intrinsic function (ISO 2002 standard or later, e.g. GnuCOBOL 2+).

code_references.snippet:
FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-NAME)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ...
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-DEPT)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ...
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-SALARY-ED)    DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ...
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-AGE-ED)       DELIMITED BY SIZE

dependencies.statement: The input physical file 'data/input/employees.dat' must exist and be accessible at runtime via the file system path relative to the program's working directory.

code_references.snippet:
SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/input/employees.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.

dependencies.statement: The output directory 'data/output/' must exist and be writable at runtime so that employees.csv can be created or overwritten.

code_references.snippet:
SELECT CSV-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/employees.csv"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.

error_handling.statement: End-of-file on EMP-FILE is handled inline within the READ statement using the AT END clause, which sets the END-OF-FILE condition-name (WS-EOF = 'Y') to terminate the processing loop gracefully. No abnormal termination or error message is issued for this condition.

code_references.snippet:
PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END PERFORM WRITE-CSV
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM

01  WS-EOF                  PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88  END-OF-FILE         VALUE 'Y'.

error_handling.statement: There is no explicit FILE STATUS, INVALID KEY, or ON EXCEPTION handling for OPEN, WRITE, or CLOSE operations on either file. Any I/O error on EMP-FILE or CSV-FILE will result in an unhandled runtime abend with a system-generated error message rather than a controlled application error.

code_references.snippet:
SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/input/employees.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
           SELECT CSV-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/employees.csv"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
OPEN INPUT EMP-FILE OUTPUT CSV-FILE

error_handling.statement: There is no overflow handling on the STRING statement. If the assembled CSV row exceeds 100 characters (the size of CSV-LINE), the STRING operation will silently truncate the output line without raising an error, potentially producing an incomplete CSV record.

code_references.snippet:
FD  CSV-FILE.
       01  CSV-LINE                PIC X(100).

MOVE 1 TO WS-PTR
           STRING EMP-ID                         DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ...
               INTO CSV-LINE WITH POINTER WS-PTR
           END-STRING

error_handling.statement: A console DISPLAY message is issued after all records are processed, providing an operator-visible record count that can be used to confirm successful completion or detect anomalies (e.g. a count of zero suggesting an empty or missing input file).

code_references.snippet: DISPLAY "CSVEXPRT: " WS-COUNT " RECORDS EXPORTED"

downstream_effects.statement: The output file 'data/output/employees.csv' is a standard comma-delimited text file with a header row. Any downstream system, report, spreadsheet tool, or ETL process that consumes employee data in CSV format can read this file. The six columns exposed are: id, name, department, salary (formatted numeric), hire_date (YYYY-MM-DD), and age.

code_references.snippet:
SELECT CSV-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/employees.csv"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.

MOVE "id,name,department,salary,hire_date,age" TO CSV-LINE
           WRITE CSV-LINE

downstream_effects.statement: The record count displayed on the console ('CSVEXPRT: NNN RECORDS EXPORTED') provides an audit trail figure that operations staff or a job scheduler can use to verify that the expected number of employee records was exported, and to reconcile against the source employees.dat file.

code_references.snippet: DISPLAY "CSVEXPRT: " WS-COUNT " RECORDS EXPORTED"
01  WS-COUNT                PIC 9(03) VALUE 0.

downstream_effects.statement: Because the output CSV-LINE field is only 100 characters wide, any downstream consumer must be aware that employee records whose concatenated field values exceed 100 characters will be silently truncated, potentially producing malformed rows in the CSV that could cause downstream parse failures.

code_references.snippet:
FD  CSV-FILE.
       01  CSV-LINE                PIC X(100).

INTO CSV-LINE WITH POINTER WS-PTR
           END-STRING
